candidate_decisions.reason: The channel nomination and the protective-disqualification HFT record describe the same bounded semantic relation: a visible, limited defect keeps a working vessel and its vulnerable owners outside a ruler's forcible seizure. The dedicated finding retains all ten channel branches, all five channel supports, the 18:79 context, and the shared focus return, so no candidate evidence is discarded.

The exact HFT trace connects the supplied 18:68 and 18:70 context to the focus question, its purpose assignment, and its verdict. The trace is complete but legacy-unbound, so its unresolved lexical branches remain attributed rather than being promoted to independent lexicon claims.

The focus breach and the supplied 18:79 explanation form an exact carrier-trigger relation: intentional visible impairment protects a livelihood-bearing vessel from indiscriminate forcible taking. All ten traced branches land, with unresolved HFT branches retained as attributed evidence.

The trace supplies the focus vessel and puncture, the later failing wall and its restoration, and the vulnerable owners and preserved wealth beneath it. These contacts support a distinct paired-boundary reading with a stated inferential boundary, while unresolved HFT branches remain attributed.

The focus sequence is repeated at 18:74 with departure, a shocking act, an accusatory question, the same coming/thing formula, and an evaluative descriptor. The recurrence changes the focus from an isolated protest to the first instance of a repeated judgment template, while preserving the live alternative that the parallel only structures escalation.

The focus vessel and breach contact the supplied 18:61 path, sea, and tunnel occurrences to form a bounded spatial resonance of reciprocal passages. The exact HFT trace names every carrier and return, but its exploratory, legacy-unbound status is retained.

The supplied 18:69, 18:73, and 18:82 occurrences return through the focus word إِمْرًا and create a distinct agency echo between grave appearance, command or affair, and the later denial of self-originated command. The trace is exploratory and attributed, not a claim that the repeated root senses collapse into one gloss.

findings.title: A visible defect protects a working vessel from seizure
findings.claim: The focus breach is re-read by 18:79 as an intentional, visible defect that keeps a livelihood-bearing vessel and its vulnerable owners from a ruler's forcible seizure.
findings.mechanism: The focus words for the ship, breach, drowning, and its people meet the 18:79 context of needy workers, intended impairment, a ruler taking every vessel, and forcible confiscation. The contact changes the hole from apparent reckless damage into a bounded disqualification that preserves the vessel's use and the people depending on it.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hold the alarming surface act together with the later protective purpose: a local loss of soundness is what prevents a larger loss of vessel, livelihood, and people.
findings.containment: The finding carries the supplied protective explanation and channel image without claiming that every defect is protective, that the ruler's selection rule is fully specified, or that the focus question was unreasonable before the later report.

epistemic.reason: The channel supports are trusted and the 18:79 relation is also supplied by a complete exact-anchor HFT trace, but the HFT record is legacy-unbound and several of its branch records have no independent lexicon gloss.

findings.title: Two boundary operations serve protection
findings.claim: The later pericope places the focus breach beside a failing wall and shows two opposed boundary operations serving protection: weaken a sound vessel when visibility invites seizure, and restore a failing wall when concealment protects vulnerable owners and their future.
findings.mechanism: The focus vessel and puncture connect through 18:79 to forcible seizure, while the wall, its imminent collapse, its restoration, orphaned owners, hidden wealth, and mercy are supplied in 18:77 and 18:82. The paired operations support a common preservation reading without making the two acts identical.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can perceive why the same narrative world contains an opening and a repair: the relevant question is what kind of boundary operation preserves the people and future behind it.
findings.containment: The common boundary calculus is an inference from the supplied opposed acts and explanations. The two incidents remain distinct, and the finding does not claim that every opening or repair follows this rule.

epistemic.reason: The HFT trace is exact and anchor-complete, but its reader identity is legacy-unbound and most branch roles have no independent lexicon record.

findings.title: The grave verdict echoes into command and agency
findings.claim: The focus word إِمْرًا keeps its grave appearance while its supplied later echoes in command, affair, and the denial of self-originated command separate the visible actor from the act's authorizing source.
findings.mechanism: The focus's grave-matter branch meets 18:69's command, 18:73's affair, and 18:82's explicit statement that the act was not from the guide's own command, with the final outcome frame in the same ayah. The repeated root relation changes a fixed moral label into an agency echo across the pericope.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can retain Musa's judgment that the act looks grave while also perceiving why the later account relocates its authority beyond the visible agent's private initiative.
findings.containment: The finding does not collapse grave matter, command, and affair into one lexical sense. It is an exploratory attributed echo that holds the surface verdict and the later agency clarification together.

epistemic.reason: The exact focus and context coordinates are supplied, but the cross-sense agency relation is an exploratory legacy-unbound HFT outlier and its context branches lack independent lexicon records.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Çekirdek anlam, büyük ve şiddetli oluşuyla yadırganan olaydır.
branch_activations.carrier: The focus descriptor carries the grave appearance of the act.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: 18:82 later denies that the guide acted from his own command.
branch_activations.activation: Grave appearance meets the later agency denial, so what is visibly judged and who authorizes it no longer coincide automatically.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The act remains grave-looking while its ultimate authorization is reopened.
branch_activations.boundary: The grave branch is not replaced by the command branch.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Çekirdek anlam, yasaklamanın karşıtı olan yapma isteği ve yükümlü kılmadır.
branch_activations.carrier: Command supplies the authority Moses promises to obey and the later command from which the guide distances himself.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The focus ends by naming the visible act a grave matter.
branch_activations.activation: Command and grave verdict meet through the same root family, creating a tension between what an act looks like and whose command authorizes it.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The focus verdict can be re-heard beside a later distinction between visible agency and authorizing command.
branch_activations.boundary: The branch remains a command relation, not a claim that the focus adjective means command.

branch_activations.facet_statement: Anlamın çekirdeği, insan işleri arasında tek tek sayılabilen konu, hal veya durumdur.
branch_activations.carrier: Musa's later appeal names the burden placed on his own affair or condition.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The focus turns the observed act into a grave matter before that later self-referential affair is discussed.
branch_activations.activation: The same root field joins the focus's classified matter to the learner's own case, widening the agency echo without replacing the focus gloss.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The verdict concerns both a grave observed matter and the human situation created by trying to judge it.
branch_activations.boundary: The focus remains the concrete act; no single lexical sense is imposed across the contexts.

branch_activations.carrier: The final account explicitly names the act as something done, supplying the visible-agent side of agency.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The immediately following denial says it was not done from the guide's own command.
branch_activations.activation: Doing and command are placed together and then separated, returning through the focus's earlier judgment of the act.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The person who performs an act need not be the private source of its authorizing command.
branch_activations.boundary: This role is attributed and does not add a general theory of agency beyond the supplied text.

branch_activations.carrier: The final return to the outcome supplies the retrospective frame in which the first verdict is re-read.
branch_activations.independent_trigger: The focus has already fixed the act as a grave matter before its later interpretation.
branch_activations.activation: Retrospective outcome meets the earlier verdict, reopening the assignment of meaning without erasing the initial appearance.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The focus's grave label remains a real first perception while later outcome changes how its agency is understood.
branch_activations.boundary: The trace does not make the later interpretation available to Musa at the moment of the focus question.
